observation: During /dso:brainstorm of epic 0777-0f3d, the cross-epic-interaction-classifier (haiku) flagged 3 signals as 'conflict' and 3 as 'ambiguity' across 5 batches of 20 epics. On manual triage by the orchestrator, only 1 of 3 'conflict' signals was a genuine mutually-exclusive conflict (4c54-4205 — blackboard extension vs blackboard removal). The other two flagged 'conflicts' (371f-cfc3 external distribution, e884-d0ad PostToolUse hook) were sequencing/coordination concerns more accurately classified as 'consideration'. Similarly, 2 of 3 'ambiguity' signals (a524-fded, 4e55-a6ba) were also more accurately 'consideration' on review; only ed62-08cd was correctly ambiguous (and on second review, was actually benign). Net: classifier escalation ratio 6/6 in the conflict/ambiguity tiers but 2/6 confirmed on triage — a 67% over-escalation rate.
recommendation: Tune the classifier prompt's four-tier rubric to be more discriminating between 'consideration' (mutually-coordinatable, integration constraint resolvable in a gate AC) and 'conflict' (mutually exclusive, one design must be reformulated). Suggested prompt addition: 'Before classifying as conflict, verify that BOTH approaches as specified cannot coexist — sequencing constraints, ordering coordination, or shared-state coordination through documented interfaces are NOT conflicts; they are considerations. Reserve conflict for cases where one epic explicitly removes/replaces a resource the other epic explicitly extends/depends on.' Also consider: include positive examples of 'consideration vs conflict' boundary cases in the agent prompt.
